newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong to spend millions on 1997 handover party.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong to spend millions on 1997 handover party.

text.p: Hong Kong will spend HK$233 million (US$30 million) on glitzy ceremonies to mark the historic handover of the British colony to China next year.

Hong Kong legislators voted 26 to three on Friday to approve the funds to pay for travel and hotels for world leaders, publicity and media facilities and a slap up reception and dinner for about 4,000 guests attending the handover ceremony itself.
At the stroke of midnight on Monday, June 30, the British flag will be lowered for the last time, marking the end of more than a century and a half of colonial rule.
The Chinese flag will be hoisted in its place followed by a new Hong Kong flag symbolising China's resumption of sovereignty over the wealthy, vibrant community of 6.3 million people.
"The ceremony will be a defining moment in the history of Hong Kong and the focus of intense international attention," a Hong Kong government statement said.
"It provides an excellent opportunity to showcase Hong Kong's strengths and success."
The opportunity to make money, one of the hallmarks of business-savvy Hong Kong, was not overlooked.
"We estimate it (the event) will bring in HK$400 to $800 million to Hong Kong's economy," Secretary for Home Affairs Michael Suen told reporters.
Not everyone approves of footing the bill for the event.
Hong Kong's largest political party, the Democratic Party abstained from the vote arguing that part of the tab should be picked up by the Chinese and the British governments.
"It looks like Hong Kong is paying the bill, while China and Britain are having the fun," Democratic Party legislator Cheung Man-kwong told reporters.
The largest slice of the HK$233 million -- HK$85 million -- will be spent on a press and broadcasting centre to cater for an estimated influx of 6,000 foreign journalists.
